newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver ends lower, gold follows suit.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver ends lower, gold follows suit.

text.p: Indian silver prices opened weak on Tuesday following a downtrend in the world market and fell further at close on fresh arrivals of imported metal, dealers said.
"Sluggish industrial buying failed to cheer sentiment," said a dealer. "Arrivals of about 800/1,000 Kg of imported silver put pressure on prices." Silver was up 55 rupees per Kg on Monday.
Gold opened on a steady note but finished lower under silver's shadow. Trading in gold remained low, delers said.
Gold biscuits (116.50 gms each) settled 200 rupees lower at 59,100 per piece. Biscuits lost 50 rupees per piece on Monday.
The Bombay bullion market remains closed on Wednesday for New Year holiday. It will re-open for trading on Thursday.
